nodes.title: Rademacher LIL constant conjecture

nodes.summary: There exist a measurable space $\Omega$, a probability measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$ and a family $(X_p)$, indexed by the primes $p$, of maps $X_p \colon \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$ into the units of $\mathbb{Z}$ that is a Rademacher family for $\mu$.
nodes.title: Existence of a Rademacher family

nodes.summary: Let $X = (X_p)$ be a family, indexed by the primes $p$, of maps $X_p \colon \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$, and let $\omega \in \Omega$. The Rademacher random multiplicative function $f$ of $X$ at $\omega$ satisfies $f(1) = 1$ and $f(mn) = f(m) f(n)$ for all coprime natural numbers $m$ and $n$.
nodes.title: The Rademacher random multiplicative function is multiplicative

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\Omega$. A family $(X_p)$, indexed by the primes $p$, of maps $X_p \colon \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$ into the units of $\mathbb{Z}$ is a Rademacher family for $\mu$ when every $X_p$ is measurable, every $X_p$ has law the Rademacher measure (the uniform measure on $\{-1, 1\}$) under $\mu$, and the family is mutually independent under $\mu$.
nodes.title: Rademacher family

nodes.summary: Let $(X_p)$ be a Rademacher family for a measure $\mu$ on a measurable space $\Omega$. For every natural number $n$, the map $\omega \mapsto \varepsilon_n(\omega)$ from $\Omega$ to $\mathbb{Z}$ is measurable, where the prime sign $\varepsilon_n(\omega)$ is $X_n(\omega)$ if $n$ is prime and $1$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Measurability of the prime signs

nodes.summary: Let $(X_p)$ be a Rademacher family for a measure $\mu$ on a measurable space $\Omega$, and for $\omega \in \Omega$ let $f_\omega$ be the Rademacher random multiplicative function of $(X_p)$ at $\omega$. For every natural number $n$, the map $\omega \mapsto f_\omega(n)$ from $\Omega$ to $\mathbb{Z}$ is measurable.
nodes.title: Measurability of the Rademacher random multiplicative function

nodes.summary: Given signs $X_p(\omega) \in \{-1, 1\}$ indexed by the primes $p$ and a sample point $\omega$, and given $N \in \mathbb{N}$, the partial sum $S_N(\omega)$ is the real number $\sum_{m=1}^{N} f_\omega(m)$, where $f_\omega$ is the Rademacher multiplicative function of the signs $X_p(\omega)$: $f_\omega(m) = \prod_{p \mid m} X_p(\omega)$ for squarefree $m$ and $f_\omega(m) = 0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Partial sums of the Rademacher multiplicative function

nodes.summary: Let $X = (X_p)$ be a family, indexed by the primes $p$, of maps $X_p \colon \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$ into the units of $\mathbb{Z}$. For a natural number $n$ and $\omega \in \Omega$, the prime sign of $n$ at $\omega$ is the integer $X_n(\omega)$ if $n$ is prime and $1$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Prime sign of a natural number

nodes.summary: Let $X = (X_p)$ be a family, indexed by the primes $p$, of maps $X_p \colon \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$, let $\omega \in \Omega$, and let $f$ be the Rademacher random multiplicative function of $X$ at $\omega$. For every natural number $n \neq 0$, $f(n) = \mu(n)^2 \prod_{p \mid n} \varepsilon_p(\omega)$, where $\mu$ is the Möbius function, the product runs over the distinct primes $p$ dividing $n$, and…
nodes.title: Formula for the Rademacher random multiplicative function

nodes.summary: Let $X = (X_p)$ be a family, indexed by the primes $p$, of maps $X_p \colon \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$, let $\omega \in \Omega$, and let $f$ be the Rademacher random multiplicative function of $X$ at $\omega$. For every squarefree natural number $n$, $f(n) = \prod_{p \mid n} \varepsilon_p(\omega)$, the product of the prime signs $\varepsilon_p(\omega)$ at $\omega$ over the distinct primes $p$ dividing $n$.
nodes.title: The Rademacher random multiplicative function on squarefree numbers

nodes.summary: Let $X = (X_p)$ be a family, indexed by the primes $p$, of maps $X_p \colon \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$, let $\omega \in \Omega$, and let $f$ be the Rademacher random multiplicative function of $X$ at $\omega$. Then $f(n) = 0$ for every natural number $n$ that is not squarefree, including $n = 0$.
nodes.title: The Rademacher random multiplicative function vanishes off squarefree numbers

nodes.summary: Let $X = (X_p)$ be a family, indexed by the primes $p$, of maps $X_p \colon \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$, let $\omega \in \Omega$, and let $f$ be the Rademacher random multiplicative function of $X$ at $\omega$. Then $f(p^2) = 0$ for every prime $p$.
nodes.title: The Rademacher random multiplicative function vanishes at prime squares

nodes.summary: Let $(X_p)_p$ be a family of maps $X_p : \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$ indexed by the primes, let $\omega \in \Omega$, and let $f$ be the associated Rademacher random multiplicative function at $\omega$. For every prime $p$, the value $f(p)$ is the sign assigned to $p$, that is, $f(p) = X_p(\omega)$.
nodes.title: Value of the Rademacher function at a prime

nodes.summary: Let $(X_p)_p$ be a family of maps $X_p : \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$ indexed by the primes, and let $\omega \in \Omega$. The Rademacher random multiplicative function at $\omega$ is the arithmetic function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ with $f(0) = 0$ and
nodes.title: Rademacher random multiplicative function

nodes.summary: For each integer unit $x \in \{-1, 1\}$, the Rademacher measure of the singleton $\{x\}$ is $1/2$.
nodes.title: Each Rademacher sign has probability one half

nodes.summary: The Rademacher measure is the uniform probability measure on the two integer units $\{-1, 1\}$.
nodes.title: Rademacher measure on the integer units

can_prove.label: ready to prove

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
